issues.title: [ROADMAP] Backend API Implementation
issues.body:
## Phase 1: Architecture Foundation

### Goal
Implement the core backend API layer that separates business logic from UI concerns.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Create `backend/api.py` with main interface functions
- [ ] Implement workout library operations
- [ ] Add movement database access methods
- [ ] Create calculation service wrappers
- [ ] Add comprehensive input validation

### API Functions to Implement
- `get_workout_library()` - Load workout categories and listings
- `get_workout_details(category, workout_id)` - Load specific workout
- `calculate_amrap(request)` - AMRAP calculation with validation
- `calculate_for_time(request)` - For Time predictions
- `get_movement_categories()` - Movement database access
- `search_movements(query)` - Movement search functionality

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All existing functionality accessible through API
- [ ] Comprehensive error handling and validation
- [ ] Type hints and documentation for all functions
- [ ] Unit tests with >90% coverage
- [ ] Performance maintained or improved vs direct calls

### Dependencies
- Depends on service layer architecture design
- Foundation for all subsequent backend work

## Phase 1: Architecture Foundation

- Return user actions/selections to parent
- Handle its own UI state management
- Follow consistent error handling patterns
- Be independently testable

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Main `streamlit_app.py` reduced to <200 lines
- [ ] All UI functionality preserved
- [ ] Components are reusable and modular
- [ ] Clear separation of concerns
- [ ] Consistent error handling across components

### Dependencies

issues.title: [ROADMAP] Database Schema Design
issues.body:
## Phase 2: Database Migration

### Goal
Design comprehensive database schema to replace JSON file storage.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Design core tables: categories, movements, workouts, workout_movements
- [ ] Add movement varieties table for flexible scaling
- [ ] Plan user tables for future authentication features
- [ ] Design proper foreign key relationships
- [ ] Create performance indexes for common queries

### Schema Components

#### Core Tables
- `categories` - Organize workouts and movements
- `movements` - Movement definitions with base timing
- `movement_varieties` - Scaling options (light/medium/heavy, etc.)
- `workouts` - Workout definitions and metadata
- `workout_movements` - Many-to-many workout-movement relationships

#### Future Tables
- `users` - User accounts and profiles
- `workout_results` - User workout history and scores
- `custom_workouts` - User-created workout definitions

### Database Design Decisions
- PostgreSQL for production reliability
- Proper normalization to 3NF
- Optimized indexes for search performance
- Foreign key constraints for data integrity
- JSON fields for flexible metadata storage

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Complete SQL schema with all tables and constraints
- [ ] Migration strategy from JSON to database
- [ ] Performance analysis and index optimization
- [ ] Data validation rules and constraints
- [ ] Documentation of all design decisions

### Dependencies
- Foundation for all database-related work
- Required before migration script development

issues.title: [ROADMAP] Migration Script Development
issues.body:
## Phase 2: Database Migration

### Goal
Create robust scripts to migrate all JSON data to database tables.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Implement `migrate_categories()` function
- [ ] Implement `migrate_movements()` with variety processing
- [ ] Implement `migrate_workouts()` with relationship handling
- [ ] Add comprehensive data validation
- [ ] Create rollback capabilities for failed migrations
- [ ] Add progress reporting and logging

### Migration Functions

#### migrate_categories()
- Load from `data/workouts/index.json` and `data/movements/index.json`
- Create category records with proper metadata
- Handle category type classification

#### migrate_movements()
- Process all `data/movements/**/*.json` files
- Create movement records with base execution times
- Create movement_varieties records for each variety
- Validate movement type and category assignments

#### migrate_workouts()
- Process all `data/workouts/**/*.json` files
- Create workout records with metadata
- Create workout_movements relationships
- Handle movement references and variety assignments

### Data Validation
- [ ] Verify all foreign key relationships
- [ ] Check for missing movement references
- [ ] Validate execution times are positive numbers
- [ ] Ensure all required fields are present
- [ ] Report data inconsistencies and warnings

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 100% of JSON data successfully migrated
- [ ] All relationships properly established
- [ ] Comprehensive validation with detailed reporting
- [ ] Rollback mechanism tested and working
- [ ] Migration performance optimized (<5 minutes)

### Dependencies
- Requires database schema to be implemented
- Foundation for service layer database integration

issues.title: [ROADMAP] Data Validation System
issues.body:
## Phase 2: Database Migration

### Goal
Implement comprehensive data validation for database integrity and application reliability.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Create input validation for all API endpoints
- [ ] Implement database constraint validation
- [ ] Add business logic validation rules
- [ ] Create data consistency checks
- [ ] Implement validation error reporting

### Validation Layers

#### Input Validation
- API request parameter validation
- Type checking and format validation
- Range validation for numeric inputs
- Required field validation

#### Database Validation
- Foreign key constraint validation
- Unique constraint enforcement
- Check constraint validation (positive times, valid types)
- Data type validation

#### Business Logic Validation
- Movement type consistency (S/D/T/M)
- Workout configuration validation
- Movement-workout compatibility checks
- Execution time reasonableness checks

### Validation Rules

#### Workout Validation
- Total time must be positive
- Multiplier must be > 0
- Rounds must be >= 1
- Time cap must be > total estimated time (warning)

#### Movement Validation
- Execution times must be positive
- Movement types must be S, D, T, or M
- Variety names must be consistent within movement
- Category references must exist

### Error Handling
- [ ] Standardized error response format
- [ ] User-friendly error messages
- [ ] Developer debugging information
- [ ] Error logging and monitoring
- [ ] Graceful degradation for non-critical errors

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All validation rules implemented and tested
- [ ] Comprehensive test coverage for edge cases
- [ ] Clear error messages for users
- [ ] Performance impact minimized
- [ ] Integration with existing error handling

### Dependencies
- Requires database schema implementation
- Integrates with migration scripts and service layer

issues.title: [ROADMAP] Django Models Implementation
issues.body:
## Phase 3: Django Backend

### Goal
Implement Django models that map to the database schema with proper relationships and validation.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Create Category model with metadata
- [ ] Create Movement model with varieties relationship
- [ ] Create MovementVariety model with execution times
- [ ] Create Workout model with configuration
- [ ] Create WorkoutMovement through model for many-to-many
- [ ] Add model validation and custom methods

### Model Specifications

#### Category Model
- Fields: key, name, description, icon, category_type
- Methods: `__str__()`, `get_workouts()`, `get_movements()`
- Validation: unique key, valid category_type

#### Movement Model
- Fields: name, slug, category, movement_type, base_execution_time
- Relationships: ForeignKey to Category, OneToMany to MovementVariety
- Methods: `get_execution_time(variety)`, `get_varieties()`
- Validation: valid movement_type (S/D/T/M), positive execution time

#### MovementVariety Model
- Fields: movement, name, execution_time, scaling_notes, is_default
- Relationships: ForeignKey to Movement
- Methods: `__str__()`, `get_scaling_info()`
- Validation: positive execution_time, one default per movement

#### Workout Model
- Fields: name, slug, description, category, workout_type, total_time, etc.
- Relationships: ManyToMany to Movement through WorkoutMovement
- Methods: `calculate_estimated_time()`, `get_movement_list()`
- Validation: positive times, valid workout_type

#### WorkoutMovement Model (Through Table)
- Fields: workout, movement, variety, count, order_position
- Methods: `get_movement_display()`, `calculate_time()`
- Validation: positive count (or -1 for max), valid order

### Django Features
- [ ] Model admin customization
- [ ] Custom model managers and querysets
- [ ] Model serialization for API
- [ ] Database migration files
- [ ] Model unit tests

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All models pass validation tests
- [ ] Relationships work correctly
- [ ] Admin interface provides full CRUD functionality
- [ ] Models integrate with existing data migration
- [ ] Performance is acceptable for expected data volumes

### Dependencies
- Requires Django project setup completion
- Uses database schema design
- Foundation for REST API development

## Phase 3: Django Backend

### Goal
Create comprehensive REST API using Django REST Framework for all application functionality.

### Technical Requirements
- [ ] Create ViewSets for all models
- [ ] Implement serializers with validation
- [ ] Add custom API endpoints for calculations
- [ ] Configure API versioning
- [ ] Add API authentication and permissions
- [ ] Create comprehensive API documentation

### API Endpoints

#### Workout Endpoints
- `GET /api/v1/workouts/` - List all workouts
- `GET /api/v1/workouts/{id}/` - Get specific workout
- `POST /api/v1/workouts/` - Create custom workout
- `GET /api/v1/categories/` - List workout categories

#### Movement Endpoints
- `GET /api/v1/movements/` - List all movements
- `GET /api/v1/movements/{id}/` - Get specific movement
- `GET /api/v1/movements/search/?q={query}` - Search movements
- `GET /api/v1/movements/{id}/varieties/` - Get movement varieties

#### Calculation Endpoints
- `POST /api/v1/calculate/amrap/` - AMRAP calculations
- `POST /api/v1/calculate/for-time/` - For Time predictions
- `POST /api/v1/validate/workout/` - Workout validation

- [ ] MovementSerializer with varieties
